evals.prompt: Redesign this dense B2B analytics dashboard to feel cleaner and more modern. We already have an established component library, typography scale, color tokens, and spacing tokens.
evals.expected_output: Triggers ui-visual-design in Standard mode. With no dashboard or design system attached, it asks for them (or inspects connected design tools) before prescribing values; any guidance is hierarchy-first, mapped to existing tokens and components, and leaves navigation and IA untouched.
expectations: Asks for the dashboard (screenshot or Figma frame) and the design system's tokens and components, or inspects them through connected tools, before prescribing any spacing, type or color value.
Every value it does give names an existing token, style or component, or is a clearly marked placeholder for a token role; it presents no raw spacing, font-size or color value as a decision.
Reads 'cleaner and more modern' as clarity (hierarchy, fewer containers, less chrome, calmer color), not as a new aesthetic.
Does not propose a new type scale, palette or visual language.
Does not copy Carbon, Material or Fluent styling.
Leaves navigation and IA unchanged, or flags any structural issue as a [DEPENDENCY].
Does not write token governance, naming conventions or component APIs.
Produces no dark-mode spec, multi-platform rules or multiple visual directions, and does not browse the web.

evals.prompt: Create the visual specification for a responsive account/settings screen that must work from compact mobile widths to large desktop, support long translated strings, RTL, dark mode, validation messages, and 200% text zoom.
evals.expected_output: Triggers ui-visual-design in Deep mode. Produces a visual spec for the responsive settings screen with per-width-range layouts, content-stress, RTL, dark-mode, validation-presentation and 200% text rules, using [PROVISIONAL] values because no design system is supplied, and flags interaction and IA decisions instead of making them.
expectations: Specifies a layout for each width range (at least compact and wide) with content priority, rather than scaling one layout.
Marks invented values such as breakpoints, spacing and type sizes as [PROVISIONAL], since no design system was supplied.
Specifies that buttons, tabs and labels size to their content and wrap instead of using fixed English-width containers.
Specifies RTL with start/end terms, mirroring the layout and directional icons but not digits, logos or checkmarks.
Describes dark mode with theme tokens and per-state contrast checks, not as inverted colors.
Presents validation errors as text plus an icon plus color at the field, with space reserved so messages don't overlap.
Does not decide when validation fires; flags it as an interaction decision.
Uses extra width on wide screens only for panes the approved structure provides, or flags [DEPENDENCY: IA]; does not invent new settings navigation.
Covers 200% text, reflow at 320 CSS px, target sizes and focus visibility.
Phrases accessibility as 'designed to address SC …' and never claims WCAG compliance.
Does not apply or browse Apple or Material guidance.

evals.prompt: Refine the high-fidelity UI of this native iOS feature. Interaction behavior is already approved. Focus only on visual presentation and platform fit.
evals.expected_output: Triggers ui-visual-design. With no screens attached it asks for them instead of inventing a feature; any guidance stays iOS-specific (Apple block only), preserves the approved interaction behavior, and contains no Material, Carbon or Fluent patterns.
expectations: Asks for the iOS screens (screenshots or Figma frames) instead of inventing a feature to refine.
Any guidance given before seeing the screens is iOS-specific, such as Dynamic Type text styles, 44 pt hit regions, SF Symbols matched to text weight, and Liquid Glass only in the functional layer.
Recommends no Material patterns: no floating action button, Material elevation or state layers, or Roboto.
Proposes no change to the approved interaction behavior or flows.
Does not read, cite or browse Material, Carbon or Fluent guidance.
Does not dump the full WCAG table or produce rules for other platforms.

evals.prompt: Our checkout form already has approved validation behavior. Design the visual presentation for default, focus, error, disabled, loading and success states.
evals.expected_output: Triggers ui-visual-design in Standard mode. Gives each of the six requested states a distinct, accessible visual treatment using token roles or [PROVISIONAL] values (no design system supplied), keeps the approved validation behavior exactly as given, and flags missing behavior as [DEPENDENCY: Interaction].
expectations: Gives a distinct visual treatment to each of the six states: default, focus, error, disabled, loading and success.
Error and success each combine text and an icon with color; no state relies on color alone.
Specifies a visible focus indicator with at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors, distinct from the error and hover treatments.
Keeps the control's dimensions during loading and reserves space for error messages so the layout doesn't shift.

Uses existing product tokens or components when supplied; since none are supplied, it names token roles or marks values [PROVISIONAL] and labels them as assumptions, or asks once for the design system.
Does not specify or change when validation fires.
Does not define retry behavior, error-recovery logic, or where focus moves after an error.
Treats any missing state or behavior as [DEPENDENCY: Interaction] instead of defining it.
Does not create component properties, variants or token architecture.
Makes no WCAG compliance claim.
Produces no responsive, dark-mode or RTL spec and does not browse platform guidance.

evals.prompt: Define when validation should fire, what happens after a failed submission, how retry works, and where focus goes after the error.
evals.expected_output: Should not trigger ui-visual-design; the primary owner is interaction-design. If the skill is invoked anyway, it names the four asks as behavior and state logic, routes them to interaction-design, and specifies none of them.
expectations: Identifies validation timing, failed-submission handling, retry and focus movement as interaction behavior.
Routes the request to interaction-design.
Does not specify when validation fires.
Does not define what happens after a failed submission or how retry works.
Does not specify where focus moves after an error.
Produces no visual state spec; any visual offer is brief and conditional on behavior decided elsewhere.
Reads no reference file and fetches no external source.

evals.prompt: We need compact, destructive, icon-only and loading versions of Button. Define the reusable component properties, variants and token architecture.
evals.expected_output: Should not trigger ui-visual-design; the primary owner is design-systems-consistency. If the skill is invoked anyway, it routes the request and, at most, lists visual requirements as inputs, defining no properties, variants or tokens.
expectations: Identifies the request as reusable component API, variant and token architecture owned by design-systems-consistency, and routes it there.
Defines no component property names or types, such as size, iconOnly or loading props, and no variant matrix.
Defines no token names, tiers or token architecture.
Does not decide between reuse, compose, extend and create.

Frames any visual requirements (destructive never styled as primary, target size kept for icon-only and compact, loading keeps dimensions, contrast kept) as inputs for design-systems-consistency, not as API decisions.
Does not audit the design system or browse the web.

evals.prompt: The developer implementation looks slightly different from Figma. Compare staging against the approved UI and tell me what should block release.
evals.expected_output: Should not trigger ui-visual-design; the primary owner is delivery-product-collaboration. If the skill is invoked anyway, it routes the build-versus-design comparison and release decision out, offering at most the approved visual intent as input.
expectations: Identifies comparing staging with Figma and deciding release blockers as implementation QA owned by delivery-product-collaboration, and routes it there.
Produces no defect list and no BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR or POLISH ratings.
Does not decide what should block release.
Limits any contribution to stating the approved visual intent as input to the QA.
Does not declare the build accessible, inaccessible or WCAG compliant.
Does not ask for staging access or screenshots in order to run the comparison itself.

evals.prompt: This pricing card feels too heavy and hard to scan. What's wrong with the visual hierarchy?
evals.expected_output: Triggers ui-visual-design in Quick mode. With no card attached it asks for it in a short message, optionally naming up to three likely causes as hypotheses; it runs no audit, adds no themes, breakpoints or platform guidance, and doesn't touch the pricing flow.
expectations: Asks for the pricing card (screenshot or frame) in a short message instead of inventing a card to critique.
Any likely causes it offers before seeing the card number three or fewer, each with a minimal fix, and are labeled as hypotheses.
Names token or style roles rather than inventing raw values.
Runs no design-system inventory or audit and produces no token tables or full specification.
Adds no dark-mode, responsive, RTL or platform guidance.
Does not browse or cite Apple, Material, Carbon or Fluent.
Does not change the plans, their order or the pricing flow.
Reads at most references/hierarchy-layout-and-density.md.
